paper.title: Gaussian Process Optimization with Adaptive Sketching: Scalable and No Regret

settings.name_in_paper: Gaussian process optimization / kernelized bandit with finite arm set (frequentist, bounded RKHS norm)
unmapped: kernel bounded: k(x,x) <= kappa^2 on all arms
settings.definition_quote: we assume that $\armset \triangleq \{\bx_i\}_{i=1}^{\Narm}$ is a fixed finite set of $\Narm$ vectors in $\Real^d$. ... receives reward $y_t \triangleq f(\bx_t) + \eta_t$, where $\eta_t$ is a zero-mean noise ... $R_T \triangleq \sum_{t=1}^T f(\bx_\star) - f(\bx_t)$ ... we additionally assume that the reward function $f$ has a bounded norm ... $\normsmall{f}_{\rkhs} \leq F$

symbols.d_eff: effective dimension Tr(K_T(K_T+lam I)^{-1}) of the arms selected by BKB up to T

conditions: noise Gaussian with variance xi^2 (xi mapped to sigma), lambda = xi^2 in the GP posterior
tuning: beta_t = 2 xi sqrt(alpha log(kappa^2 t) sum_s sigma_tilde_t^2(x_s) + log(1/delta)) + (1 + 1/sqrt(1-eps)) sqrt(lambda) F

source.label: thm:main-regret
source.quote: Assume $\normsmall{f}_{\rkhs} \leq F < \infty$. For any desired $0 < \varepsilon < 1$, $0 < \delta < 1$, $0 < \lambda$, let $\alpha \triangleq (1 + \varepsilon)/(1 - \varepsilon)$ and $\qbar \geq 6\alpha\log(4T/\delta)/\varepsilon^2$. If we run \bkb with ... then, with probability of at least $1-\delta$, the regret $R_T$ of \bkb is bounded as R_T \leq 2(2\alpha)^{3/2}\sqrt{T}(\xi\deff(\lambda,\wt{\bX}_T)\log(\kappa^2T) +\sqrt{\lambda \fnorm^2 \deff(\lambda,\wt{\bX}_T)\log(\kappa^2T)}+ \xi\log(1/\delta))

results.notes: d_eff is data-dependent (evaluated on the arms played). The paper's noise is Gaussian with std xi; it notes sub-Gaussian noise also works. Regret is realized regret in f-values, holding w.p. 1-delta. Theorem 1 (dictionary size / variance accuracy) is a computational guarantee and not recorded.
